correctness.rationale: On the common-intersection orthogonal complement, the products are weakly null and have nonincreasing norms. At every recurrent-word endpoint, the vector is the compact operator W-P applied to a bounded weakly null vector, so a norm-null subsequence is forced; monotonicity then gives full strong convergence. The finite-excess and strict two-letter examples were checked directly.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2026 infinite-periodic source proves weak convergence and a positivity-based strong criterion but contains no compactness, finite-dimensional-excess, or Calkin criterion. Earlier countable work gives weak-plus-strong-subsequence and angle/tail criteria. Classical compact random-product results found are for finite generating families; no inspected source states the recurrent compact-word criterion or its countably infinite application.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a reusable operator-ideal mechanism that upgrades the new countably infinite weak-convergence theorem to strong convergence. Its one-letter form is a simple finite-excess geometric criterion, while the explicit two-letter construction shows the mechanism genuinely goes beyond requiring any individual reduced projection to be compact.
